title: Oct 2026 (Madinah)
des: Saudi Prometric paediatrics recall, Madinah, October 2026 (exact day not stated)

questions.question: A child after a road accident has organised electrical activity on the monitor but no pulse. What is given?
questions.exp: PEA is non-shockable; look for hypovolaemia, tamponade, tension pneumothorax.

questions.question: A child who took a decongestant has HR 200 with SVT. What is the treatment if stable?
A child with hyperkalaemia has paraesthesia. What is given first?
A child took his father's medicine and has HR 52 with vomiting. What drug is most likely?
questions.exp: Bradycardia, vomiting, visual changes; give digoxin-specific Fab.

questions.question: What is a common complication of tetralogy of Fallot?
Which cyanotic lesion has oligaemic lung fields?
In which infants does indomethacin close a PDA more effectively?
questions.exp: The preterm duct is sensitive to prostaglandin inhibition; in term infants the duct wall is structurally abnormal.

questions.question: A child has wide fixed splitting of S2. What is the diagnosis?
A 9-month-old with a 9-mm VSD is on full heart failure treatment and still failing. What is next?
What is the most common cause of infective endocarditis in children?
An adolescent with rheumatic heart disease who injects drugs develops endocarditis. What is the organism?
A child has breathlessness, bone pain, a new murmur and hepatosplenomegaly. What is the diagnosis?
A child has migratory arthritis from the knee to other large joints. What is the diagnosis?
What is the treatment of pyelonephritis needing IV therapy?
questions.exp: Nitrofurantoin does not treat renal infection. The recall writer chose cefazolin.

questions.question: A child has haematuria, high BP and raised ASOT after a throat infection. What is the treatment?
questions.a: Fluid and salt restriction with diuretic and antihypertensive (calcium channel blocker)

questions.question: A 1-year-old on a constipating drug has UTI. How is urine collected?
A child has cystitis with new night wetting and lower abdominal pain, without fever. What is the treatment?
A child with atypical HUS needs dialysis but parents refuse. What should be done?
questions.a: Give dialysis in the child's best interest

questions.question: A child with membranoproliferative GN remains nephrotic after 6 weeks of steroids. What is next?
questions.exp: Steroid resistance: biopsy and calcineurin inhibitors.

questions.question: A child has polyuria, polydipsia, low sodium and chloride, high urine chloride and metabolic alkalosis. What is the diagnosis?
A child has high urea, creatinine, phosphate and ALP with bone changes. What should be measured to stage the disease?
A child has daytime wetting with urgency and voids 10-15 times a day. What should be excluded first?
A toddler cries when left with a babysitter. What is this?
A 2-year-old bites everyone. What is the advice?
questions.a: Consistent response with positive reinforcement of good behaviour

questions.question: A baby is born to an HBsAg-positive mother. What is given?
questions.d: HBIG and hepatitis B vaccine within 12 hours

questions.question: A stable child with a recent focal seizure is due vaccines. What should be done?
questions.exp: Stable neurological conditions are not a contraindication; defer DTaP only for progressive encephalopathy.

questions.question: A child has a clean minor wound and the mother does not know his tetanus status. What is given?
questions.exp: Clean minor wounds need vaccine only; TIG for dirty wounds with unknown status.

questions.question: A 6-month-old had anaphylaxis to his 4-month vaccines. What is next?
What responds first to iron therapy?
A child with sickle cell disease has transcranial Doppler velocity above 200 cm/s twice. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: STOP trial: chronic transfusion prevents stroke.

questions.question: Which clotting factors depend on vitamin K?
What is cryoprecipitate rich in?
A newborn has umbilical stump bleeding with normal PT and PTT. What is the most likely deficiency?
questions.exp: Normal screening tests; also intracranial bleeding.

questions.question: A child has new and old petechiae on the legs and palate after a URTI with low platelets. What is the diagnosis?
A child rides a tricycle but cannot copy a square. What is the age?
questions.exp: Tricycle and circle at 3; square at 4.

questions.question: A child has seborrhoeic-like dermatitis not responding to treatment, hepatosplenomegaly and lytic skull lesions. What is the diagnosis?
A male has hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism and anosmia. What is the diagnosis?
A 13-year-old girl has a webbed neck and height 115 cm. What is the investigation?
A child has upslanting eyes, flat face and single palmar crease. What is the diagnosis?
How is Down syndrome confirmed?
An infant has hypotonia and tongue fasciculations. What is the test?
A newborn becomes cyanosed when feeding and improves when crying. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: Pass a catheter first, then CT.

questions.question: A child with ALL has a perianal lesion. What is the empirical treatment?
A child with ALL has bloody diarrhoea. Which infection is suspected?
questions.exp: The recall writer chose aspergillosis from a picture.

questions.question: A child with ALL has neutrophils 0.1 and fever. What is the empirical treatment?
A 10-year-old with meningitis has Gram-positive diplococci in CSF. What is the treatment?
A child has scarlet fever with strawberry tongue. What is the organism?
A ventilated neonate has late-onset sepsis. What is the empirical treatment?
A 3-month-old in ICU develops a central line infection. What is the empirical treatment?
A 4-month-old with RSV has repeated apnoeas and desaturation but improves with oxygen. Where should he be managed?
questions.exp: Recurrent apnoea is an indication for intensive care. The recall writer chose the ward.

questions.question: A child with portal hypertension and ascites has peritonitis. What is the most likely organism?
A child is colonised with MRSA. What should be done?
What are airborne precautions?
How is bacterial parotitis diagnosed?
questions.b: Culture of pus from the parotid duct

questions.question: An infant of a diabetic mother is at risk of which problem?
A newborn has temperature 29 °C. Which finding is expected?
During resuscitation of a hypothermic preterm newborn, which action does NOT help with warming?
questions.exp: Plastic wrap and warmer prevent heat loss.

questions.question: After otitis media a child has middle ear effusion. What is the management?
questions.c: Watchful waiting with review in about 3 months

questions.question: What is the treatment of acute otitis media?
questions.exp: 10 days under 2 years, 5-7 days in older children.
questions.b: Amoxicillin 80-90 mg/kg/day for 10 days in young children

questions.question: A child with otitis media becomes irritable. What is the next step?
A diabetic child has white membranes in the mouth. What is the diagnosis?
A child has itchy purple polygonal flat-topped papules with white streaks. What is the diagnosis?
A newborn has a skin-covered occipital sac. What is the diagnosis?
A child has chronic cough, negative TB test and erythema nodosum. What is the diagnosis?
An infant has bone pain (pseudoparalysis) and peeling skin. What is the diagnosis?
A child has oedema, low albumin and peeling dry skin. What is the diagnosis?
A short child with a high-pitched voice has GH deficiency. What is the treatment?
A 115-cm child has an ejection murmur at the right upper sternal border. What is the lesion?
A child has a tension pneumothorax with BP 70/35. What is the first step?
Which pneumonia needs a follow-up X-ray?
A child has stridor and drooling. What is done to secure the airway?
questions.exp: The recall writer chose nasotracheal intubation.
questions.b: Intubation in theatre by experienced staff

questions.question: A child has a brassy cough, high fever and toxicity. What is the diagnosis?
What is the length gain per month in months 3-6?
An infant has macrocephaly with normal feeding. What is the investigation?
A child with IBD has clubbing and active colitis. What is the treatment for a flare?
questions.a: Oral prednisolone (or exclusive enteral nutrition in Crohn)

questions.question: A child with atopy has spasmodic night-time croup. What is the diagnosis?
A teenager in a body cast for scoliosis develops bilious vomiting. What is the diagnosis?
A newborn has a scalp swelling crossing the midline present at birth. What is it?
Which renal tumour has the worst prognosis?
A child has intractable seizures and hypopigmented macules. What is the diagnosis?
A hyperactive boy has falling school performance and skin pigmentation. What is the investigation?
What is the most common oesophageal foreign body in children?
Why are young children more exposed to toxins such as lead dust?
questions.b: They are closer to the ground and put things in their mouths

questions.question: A child with developmental delay eats everything from the ground. What should be checked?
What is the EEG finding of infantile spasms?
A child has a URTI every month but grows well. What is the management?
A toddler has gratification behaviour. What is the management?
A child with dermatomyositis features is evaluated. What test?
An infant with bruises from non-accidental injury has drowsiness. What is the likely bleed?
A child was well after head trauma, then lost consciousness an hour later. What is the diagnosis?
What is a serious colonic complication of IBD?
A child has weight loss and anorexia without melaena; endoscopy and histology are diagnostic. What is the organism?
A child has bounding pulses, capillary refill 1 second and low BP. What is the shock type?
A child has a nasal mass or foreign body with orbital swelling. What is the investigation?
A child has an intranasal mass. What imaging is needed before biopsy?
A 10-year-old falls from a horse with leg weakness and no X-ray abnormality. What is the investigation?
A child after diarrhoea develops encephalopathy with neurological signs. What is the investigation?
A child has acute leg weakness with a positive Babinski. What is the diagnosis?
What does MRI show in transverse myelitis?
questions.a: Cord T2 signal with gadolinium enhancement

questions.question: A 2-year-old has Na 170 mmol/L, fever and BP 110 after diarrhoea. What is the diagnosis?
Which treatment reduces cerebral oedema?
A child has constipation with soiling and low anal tone on examination. What is the most important concern?
questions.exp: Reduced anal tone is a red flag. The recall writer chose functional constipation.
questions.b: Spinal cord lesion; examine the back and lower limbs

questions.question: A 2-week-old has milky then bilious vomiting with a normal rectal exam. What is the diagnosis?
In suspected midgut volvulus, what is the management?
questions.d: IV fluids and urgent upper GI contrast

questions.question: A 2-week-old has a gush of stool after rectal examination. What is the diagnosis?
A child has retching without vomiting and the NG tube cannot pass. What is the management?
A child after Hirschsprung surgery has abdominal pain and distension. What is the treatment?
questions.a: Rectal irrigation with warm saline and antibiotics

questions.question: A child has maroon stool. What is the investigation?
A 7-week-old has projectile non-bilious vomiting with hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis. Which fluid is used first?
What acid-base disturbance is typical of cystic fibrosis?
Which condition causes a false negative Mantoux?
Which condition causes a false negative sweat chloride test?
A child has diarrhoea and stool positive for reducing substances. What is the cause?
An infant has diarrhoea and vomiting after starting jarred fruit. Which enzyme is deficient?
A child on antibiotics has severe diarrhoea needing admission. What is the likely cause?
A doctor interrupts a nurse and dismisses her input. What is this?
An error is caught before it reaches the patient. What is this?
A wrong digoxin dose was given and the patient died. What should be done?
questions.b: Disclose the error honestly to the parents

questions.question: A doctor works in both private and government sectors at the same time against rules. Which principle is breached?
A girl has vaginal bleeding and unexplained bruises. What must be considered?
A child with a bone-anchored hearing aid had an error in care. How should it be reviewed?
During an H1N1 outbreak a citizen refuses public health measures. Which principle applies?
What is procedural justice?
questions.c: Fair processes following laws and regulations

questions.question: A senior teaches comprehensive professionalism and faithfulness to duties. Which principle?
A programme gives free vaccination only to non-smokers. What is this?
A researcher does not inform participants of side effects. What is breached?
Which practice improves patient safety before procedures and treatment?
An electronic system refuses a prescription with missing data. What is this?
What is the best imaging for neuronal migration disorders?
A child was in a fire. What should be measured?
How is long-term glycaemic control monitored in diabetes?
A child has convulsed for 40 minutes with temperature 38.6 °C. What is this?
A 10-month-old has a persistent left eye deviation. What is the management?
questions.exp: Constant squint after 4-6 months needs assessment.

questions.question: How is pain assessed in children?
A child has a recurrent simple febrile seizure. What is the management?
A child has a seizure followed by 30 minutes of post-ictal drowsiness without fever. What is the investigation?
A child has recurrent periumbilical pain with pallor, normal between episodes. What is the diagnosis?
A child has recurrent throbbing headaches with photophobia. What is the diagnosis?
Which medicine can treat severe tics?
A toddler has breath-holding spells. What is the management?
A child has pancytopenia and dark complexion. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: The recall writer chose bone marrow biopsy.
questions.d: Chromosomal breakage test and bone marrow biopsy

questions.question: A child has vomiting and blood-tinged diarrhoea with oliguria. Which test distinguishes pre-renal failure?
An asthmatic child had one PICU admission. What is the preventer?
How is epistaxis managed first?
questions.b: Lean forward and compress the nose

questions.question: A child on inhaled steroids has epistaxis. What is the likely cause?
questions.d: Allergic rhinitis with steroid-related mucosal irritation

questions.question: A child has pale boggy swollen nasal mucosa. What is the treatment?
What is an indication for tonsillectomy?
questions.b: Recurrent severe tonsillitis (7 in 1 year, 5/year for 2 years, 3/year for 3 years)

questions.question: A well 2-week-old breastfed baby has total bilirubin 174 µmol/L, mostly indirect. What is the management?
questions.d: Reassure (breast milk jaundice), checking thyroid and conjugated level

questions.question: A baby has raised conjugated bilirubin. What is the first question?
What does the trauma secondary survey include?
A child has frequent falls and low IgA and IgG. What test?
What is the best psychotherapy for childhood anxiety or depression?
A child has soiling with impaction. What is first?
A child has constipation and dry skin. What should be checked?
A 13-year-old girl has an abdominal mass and no menarche. What is the investigation?
A child has sudden unilateral facial weakness including the forehead. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: LMN facial palsy; steroids within 72 hours.

questions.question: What is true about umbilical hernia in infants?
questions.a: Strangulation is rare and most close by 4-5 years

questions.question: A meconium-stained baby is not breathing. What is done?
questions.d: Start positive-pressure ventilation with bag and mask

questions.question: A pleural fluid has protein 35 g/L. What type is it?
A child wakes screaming early in the night with no memory. What is it?
A child snores. What is the investigation?
An ABG shows low pH, high PaCO2 and low PaO2. What is it?
A child has recurrent left lower lobe pneumonia with a lesion supplied by a systemic artery. What is it?
A girl has hand wringing and regression. What is the test?
A child needs hepatitis A vaccine. What should be done?
How long is penicillin given for streptococcal pharyngitis?
What is the most common cause of haematuria in children?
questions.exp: UTI and trauma are common causes.

questions.question: A child has dark red urine with no red cells on microscopy. What is the cause?
An infant has RSV bronchiolitis, is distressed and has not had saturation measured. What is next?
questions.b: Measure SpO2 and give oxygen if below 90-92%

questions.question: A patient has double vision looking left that disappears when the right eye is covered, with the outer image from the left eye. Which nerve is affected?
questions.exp: Diplopia worse in the direction of the weak lateral rectus. The recall was unclear.
